title: Identify the prescribed pro-etale scalar/direct-image mate with the ringed-topos mate
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a unital map $\varphi:A\to B$ of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$, and an arbitrary morphism of schemes $q:Z\to Y$. Use the ordinary unbounded constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and exactly the geometric adjunctions $P_R=q_R^*\dashv G_R=Rq_{*,R}$ for $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with counits $\varepsilon^R$. Set $T_T^{A,B}=(-)\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Let $\lambda_q:P_BT_Y^{A,B}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Z^{A,B}P_A$ and $\gamma_q:T_Y^{A,B}G_A\to G_BT_Z^{A,B}$ be the balanced K-flat pullback isomorphism and its specified counit mate [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison].

Put $u=q_{\mathrm{proet}}$. On $Z$ first use the literal ring sheaves $u^{-1}A_Y,u^{-1}B_Y$ with ring map $u^{-1}(\varphi_Y)$. Let $\widetilde\lambda$ be their canonical inverse-image/tensor comparison and $\chi_\varphi$ its counit mate, with exactly the conventions of [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle]. Transport their module actions, functors, and transformations through the canonical ring isomorphisms $c_R:u^{-1}R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}R_Z$ adjoint to constant sections [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison]. The transported geometric adjunctions agree with the normalized $P_R\dashv G_R$, including their counits, and the transported $\widetilde\lambda$ equals $\lambda_q$ as a natural transformation. On K-flat representatives their ordinary maps both take the inverse image of $x\otimes b$ to the inverse image of $x$ tensor $b$.

Consequently the transported $\chi_\varphi$ equals $\gamma_q$ as a natural transformation, with the following common, unique counit-transpose characterization for every $E\in D(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$:
$$\varepsilon^B_{T_Z^{A,B}E}\circ P_B(\gamma_{q,E})=T_Z^{A,B}(\varepsilon^A_E)\circ\lambda_{q,G_AE}.$$
All identifications are natural in $E$, and the assertions hold for arbitrary $q$ and arbitrary unbounded $E$, without flatness, finite projective dimension, or invertibility of the direct-image comparison. No different choice of geometric adjunction or of coefficient comparison is allowed.

proof.text:
Write $\widehat R=u^{-1}R_Y$ for $R=A,B$. The canonical maps $c_R:\widehat R\to R_Z$ are ring isomorphisms by [lem-pur-proetale-constant-coefficient-comparison]. They respect the specified coefficient homomorphism:
$$c_B\circ u^{-1}(\varphi_Y)=\varphi_Z\circ c_A.$$
Indeed, under the ring-sheaf adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the adjuncts of both sides are the map $A_Y\to u_*B_Z$ sending a constant section $a$ to the constant section $\varphi(a)$. They agree before sheafification and hence on the constant sheaf. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the equality. Thus every change of action below uses the given $\varphi$, not a separately selected identification.

source.place: Tag 0H7J (example-constant-sheaf); the constant-section maps of def-weil-proetale-inverse-image

proof.text:
For a $\widehat R$-module $N$, let $J_RN$ be the same abelian sheaf with $R_Z$-action $r n=c_R^{-1}(r)n$; the inverse equivalence restricts the action along $c_R$. These functors leave maps, kernels and cokernels unchanged. The tensor presentation of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is identified with $J_Ru^{-1}F$ by
$$u^{-1}F\otimes_{\widehat R,c_R}R_Z\longrightarrow J_Ru^{-1}F,\qquad m\otimes r\longmapsto c_R^{-1}(r)m,$$
with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. Balancing proves both composite identities, and the formulas commute with restriction. On direct image the action of $R_Y$ is through the adjunct of $c_R$, namely the map $\rho_R$ defining [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Thus the transported literal direct image is exactly the specified ordinary direct image. The module Hom bijection in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] is the underlying sheaf Hom bijection in both presentations; consequently these identifications preserve its unit and evaluation counit, not merely its functors.

source.place: Tag 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); transport along an invertible structural ring map

proof.text: First compare the two definitions of the literal derived adjunction. With coefficients $(R_Y,\widehat R)$ and structural map $1_{\widehat R}$, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] has the same exact ordinary inverse image and K-injective right-derived direct image as the canonical ringed adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Their canonical derived Hom bijections agree: if $I$ is K-injective, then $u_*I$ is K-injective, since for an acyclic $L$ the termwise adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_K(L,u_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_K(u^{-1}L,I)=0$ by exactness of $u^{-1}$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies both derived Hom sets with their homotopy Hom sets. Both canonical bijections are the ordinary termwise adjunction there, by the representing-fraction formula of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] (take the identity resolution maps at $I$ and at a homotopy representative of the source). Every target has a K-injective resolution by the constructions in the cited operations. Their naturality therefore identifies the bijections on every target, including the image of its identity morphism, which is its counit.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint); derived.tex Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), with the canonical pre-derived Hom formula

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] separately for $R=A,B$. In its notation take $R_V=S_V=R_Y$, $R_U=\widehat R$, $S_U=R_Z$, $a_V=1$, $a_U=c_R$, and structural isomorphisms $c_{\rm old}=1_{\widehat R}$ and $c_{\rm new}=c_R$. Its required compatibility is $c_R\circ1=c_R\circ u^{-1}(1)$. Its $r_U$ is the inverse of $J_R$ from step 2 and $r_V$ is the identity. The theorem gives natural derived pullback and direct-image comparisons and says explicitly that they preserve adjuncts. By step 3 the old adjunction is the literal ringed one. By step 2 the new one is precisely the prescribed constant-ring adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. To see the counit normalization directly in the theorem's formula, take $M=G_R E$, $N=E$ and $t=\varepsilon^R_E$. Its adjunct is $1_{G_RE}$; the displayed compatibility says that the old counit becomes $\varepsilon^R_E$ after the specified comparisons. Thus these are identifications of the normalized adjunctions, including counits, on the entire unbounded categories.

For an $A_Y$-module $F$, [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] gives the unique ordinary inverse-image tensor comparison
$$u^{-1}(F\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)\longrightarrow u^{-1}F\otimes_{\widehat A}\widehat B,\qquad u^{-1}(x\otimes b)\longmapsto u^{-1}x\otimes u^{-1}b.$$
After step 2's action identifications, the right side is identified with $q_A^*F\otimes_{A_Z}B_Z$ by $m\otimes b'\mapsto m\otimes c_B(b')$. This is balanced: the relation $(a'm)\otimes b'=m\otimes u^{-1}\varphi_Y(a')b'$ becomes $(c_A(a')m)\otimes c_B(b')=m\otimes\varphi_Z(c_A(a'))c_B(b')$ by step 1. Its inverse uses $c_B^{-1}$. The same formulas on the left identify its transported sheaf with $q_B^*(F\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y)$. Thus the resulting comparison sends the inverse image of $x\otimes b$ to $q_A^*x\otimes c_B(u^{-1}b)$; in particular a constant $b$ is sent to the same constant $b$. This is exactly the ordinary balanced map prescribed in [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison]. The cited uniqueness proves equality of sheaf maps, as opposed to merely equality of their induced cohomology maps.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), with the pure-tensor and coefficient-naturality normalization

proof.text: For any $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ choose a K-flat representative $P$ with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Scalar extension is represented by $P\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y$ by [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to the literal geometric morphism, its identified-coefficient version, and the identity-topos coefficient morphism shows that $u^{-1}P$, $q_A^*P$, and $P\otimes_{A_Y}B_Y$ have the required K-flat, flat-term models over their respective rings. Both geometric pullbacks are exact by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Consequently the two composite derived functors in the comparison are represented by the two sides of step 5 applied termwise to $P$; this involves no flatness of $B$ over $A$. The equality of their ordinary maps in each degree is compatible with differentials and chain maps, since its formula is natural in $F$. It therefore gives equality after localization. The K-flat localization equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] shows that this is equality of natural transformations on the whole derived category, independent of the representative. In particular the transported $\widetilde\lambda$ equals the specified $\lambda_q$, with its $B_Z$-action.

Denote the transported $\chi_\varphi$ by $h:T_Y^{A,B}G_A\to G_BT_Z^{A,B}$. Use the definition of $\chi$ in [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-projection-cocycle], with coefficient chain $A_Y\xrightarrow{\varphi_Y}B_Y\xrightarrow{1}B_Y$. Step 4 identifies its counits and step 6 identifies its inverse-image/tensor comparison, so its defining adjunct is
$$v_E=T_Z^{A,B}(\varepsilon^A_E)\circ\lambda_{q,G_AE}.$$
By [def-sp-reduction-direct-image-comparison], $\gamma_{q,E}$ has this same adjunct. Explicitly, for $X=T_Y^{A,B}G_AE$, $Y=T_Z^{A,B}E$, the adjunction bijection sends $k:X\to G_BY$ to $\varepsilon^B_Y\circ P_B(k)$, and its inverse sends $v:P_BX\to Y$ to $G_B(v)\circ\eta^B_X$. The two triangle identities make these inverse functions. Thus $h_E=\gamma_{q,E}$ and both satisfy the displayed counit identity, which also characterizes them uniquely. All preceding comparisons and $v_E$ are natural, so this equality is an equality of natural transformations. K-flat and K-injective resolutions used above exist for arbitrary unbounded complexes; no step uses properness of $q$, finite projective dimension, or invertibility of $h_E$.
